source.author: cic
source.text: Quo quidem ipso in loco multa a Crasso divinitus dicta esse ferebantur, cum sibi illum consulem esse negaret, cui senator ipse non esset.
source.text_original: Quo quidem ipso in loco multa a Crasso divinitus dicta esse ferebantur, cum sibi illum consulem esse negaret, cui senator ipse non esset.
source.text_english: At that very point, indeed, many things were said by Crassus with divine inspiration, when he denied that he himself was a senator to that consul to whom he was not one.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: scitum illud est oratoris Domitii: ego te, inquit, habeam ut principem, cum tu me non habeas ut senatorem?
reuse.text_original: scitum illud est oratoris Domitii: ego te, inquit, habeam ut principem, cum tu me non habeas ut senatorem?
reuse.text_english: There is that famous saying of the orator Domitius: Do you want me to regard you as princeps, when you do not regard me as a senator?
